subject: Science
title: Where animals live
objectives: Children will match animals to their homes.
Children will say simple words for animal homes.
content: Homes of farm animals, homes of wild animals, and matching animals to their homes.
teachingActivities: Show the home picture first, then the animal; use words nest, pen, kennel and hole; build a small farm with boxes; link to what children see near the school.
learnerActivities: Match animals to their homes and say a word for each home.
resources: Pictures of a nest, a pen, a kennel, a hole and a tree
Animal pictures: hen, goat, dog, rabbit, monkey
assessment: Observe whether each child matches at least three animals to homes and names one animal home.
expectedOutcomes: Matches at least three animals to their homes.

lessons.title: Homes on the farm
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will match farm animals to their homes.
successCriteria: Matches the hen to the nest and the dog to the kennel
Says the name of one home
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals and say if they are pets or wild.
resources: Pictures of a nest, pen and kennel
Pictures of a hen, a goat and a dog
lessons.starter: Show a kennel picture and say "This is a kennel. A dog sleeps here." Ask "Where does the dog live?"
teacherActivities: Show each home picture and say its name.
Show an animal picture and ask "Where does it live?"
Put each animal in its home box.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the name.
Child points to the home.
Child places the animal in the right box.
Child says hen or bird.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each home picture and say its name. Children: Children look and say the name.
Step 2. Teacher: Show an animal picture and ask "Where does it live?" Children: Child points to the home.
Step 3. Teacher: Put each animal in its home box. Children: Child places the animal in the right box.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Who lives in the nest?" Children: Child says hen or bird.

practical.title: Farm homes
steps: Put three home boxes on the mat.
Each child picks an animal toy.
practical.safety: Use clean soft toys and large boxes. Keep the floor clear and supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Offer two homes and show the animal first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what the animal does at home.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Matches farm animals to their homes
lessons.conclusion: Put the animals in their homes and say goodnight.
lessons.homeConnection: Look at where animals live near your home and name the homes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match farm animals to their homes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Homes in the wild
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will match wild animals to their homes.
successCriteria: Matches a monkey to a tree and a rabbit to a hole
Says the name of one wild home
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals and say if they are pets or wild.
resources: Pictures of a tree, a hole, water and a cave
Pictures of a monkey, a rabbit, a fish and a bat
lessons.starter: Show a tree picture and say "A monkey lives in a tree." Ask "Who lives in a tree?"
teacherActivities: Show each home picture and say its name.
Show an animal and ask "Where does it live?"
Talk about how animals find food and water in their homes.
Let each child match one animal to its home.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the name.
Child points to the home.
Children listen and point to food and water pictures.
Child places an animal on its home.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each home picture and say its name. Children: Children look and say the name.
Step 2. Teacher: Show an animal and ask "Where does it live?" Children: Child points to the home.
Step 3. Teacher: Talk about how animals find food and water in their homes. Children: Children listen and point to food and water pictures.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child match one animal to its home. Children: Child places an animal on its home.

practical.title: Wild homes
steps: Put home pictures on the floor.
Each child takes an animal card.
Stand the animal on its home.
practical.safety: Use large cards on a clear floor. Supervise movement and turns.

differentiation.support: Offer two homes and say the animal first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find where fish live and say why.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put all the animals back in their homes.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for animal homes outside, such as nests and holes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match wild animals to their homes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Matching homes game
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will play a matching game with animals and homes.
successCriteria: Matches at least three animals to homes
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals and say if they are pets or wild.
lessons.starter: Say "Let us help the animals find their homes. Who is missing a home?"
teacherActivities: Spread out the home cards. Pick an animal and ask "Where does it live?"
Match the card and say the animal and the home.
Let each child pick an animal from the bag and match it.
learnerActivities: Child points to the home.
Children say both words.
Child picks and matches.
Children name the pairs.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Spread out the home cards. Pick an animal and ask "Where does it live?" Children: Child points to the home.
Step 2. Teacher: Match the card and say the animal and the home. Children: Children say both words.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick an animal from the bag and match it. Children: Child picks and matches.
Step 4. Teacher: Check all the pairs together. Children: Children name the pairs.

practical.title: Home match
steps: Put six home cards on the mat.
Each child picks an animal card.
practical.safety: Use large soft cards. Supervise turns and keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Use three pairs only and say the home first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to match all six pairs alone.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the cards away and say "All the animals are home."
lessons.homeConnection: Play animal home matching with pictures at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play a matching game with animals and homes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Building a farm
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will build a model farm with homes for animals.
successCriteria: Builds a home for an animal
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals and say if they are pets or wild.
lessons.starter: Show the toy animals and say "The animals need homes. Let us build a farm."
teacherActivities: Show how to build a pen with blocks and a nest with cloth.
Let each child build a home for an animal.
Put the animals in their new homes.
Walk round and ask "What did you build?"
learnerActivities: Children watch and choose a block.
Child builds a home with blocks or boxes.
Child places an animal in a home.
Child says the name of the home.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to build a pen with blocks and a nest with cloth. Children: Children watch and choose a block.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child build a home for an animal. Children: Child builds a home with blocks or boxes.
Step 3. Teacher: Put the animals in their new homes. Children: Child places an animal in a home.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk round and ask "What did you build?" Children: Child says the name of the home.

practical.title: Farm building
steps: Set out blocks, boxes and cloth.
practical.safety: Use soft blocks and keep towers low. Clear the floor and supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Build beside the child and name each part.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to build a home with a roof and a door.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Builds a home for an animal
lessons.conclusion: Look at the farm together and say "Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Build a home for a toy animal at home with boxes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "build a model farm with homes for animals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 2 homes check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child matches animals to homes.
successCriteria: Matches at least three animals to homes
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals and say if they are pets or wild.
lessons.starter: Say "Where do animals live?" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: farm homes, wild homes and building.
At each station ask "Where does the animal live?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child points to or names the home.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: farm homes, wild homes and building. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Where does the animal live?" Children: Child points to or names the home.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Home stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use soft toys and large cards.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two homes.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a friend where animals live.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: matches animals to homes; names one home; builds a home.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
lessons.conclusion: Say goodnight to the animals in their homes.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about animal homes whenever you see animals.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child matches animals to homes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
